tasks.extracted: Nonlinear Mendelian randomization with the primary score: quadratic models fitted best for coronary artery disease and hypertension (P < .001), with every amount of intake associated with higher risk, rising more steeply at higher intake; the fitted curves print no values. With the secondary score (10 variants for the AUDIT-C consumption score), piecewise analyses suggested no rise in cardiovascular risk until roughly 7 to 14 drinks a week, with slight decreases at modest intake for hypertension and in some analyses in women, which the authors attribute to pleiotropy in that score and low power.

tasks.source_read: PMC full text PMC8956974 with correction notice PMC9021906, as read for card sc_biddinger_2022: all sections, Tables 1 and 2; Figures 1 to 3 read only approximately; supplement not read
tasks.extracted: The score was not associated with the outcomes in 34,423 lifelong abstainers, except for HDL cholesterol and apolipoprotein A, which the authors call a potential pleiotropic effect; MR-Egger intercepts were non-significant. The authors acknowledge that the associations may reflect genes that influence both drinking and cardiovascular disease rather than an effect of alcohol, and that variants for diagnosed alcohol use disorder are an indirect proxy for usual intake.
